Coordinated describes something — or someone — where multiple parts work together smoothly and effectively, each doing its own job in a way that fits with what the others are doing.

Think of a marching band. Every musician plays a different instrument, every person moves in a different position on the field — yet everything happens at the right time, in the right place, in the right order. Nothing is clashing or out of sync. That is what coordinated means: organized harmony between different parts.
The Three Main Ways It's Used

1. Actions or efforts that are planned and carried out together

This is the most common use. When multiple people, groups, or elements act together in a planned, organized way — especially to achieve a shared goal — we call it a coordinated effort.

"The government launched a coordinated response to the flood — the army, the hospitals, and the relief teams all knew exactly what to do and when."

"The rival gangs carried out a coordinated attack on three locations at the same time."

The key idea here is intentional synchronization. It's not just that many things are happening — it's that they are happening in a deliberately organized, mutually supporting way. If the flood response had each team acting on its own without any shared plan, it would be uncoordinated.

Notice that "coordinated" in this sense carries a sense of efficiency and planning. It implies someone (or a group) took the trouble to align the parts so they don't conflict and don't duplicate each other's work.

2. Physical control of the body

When we say a person is coordinated, we mean their body moves in a smooth, controlled, and skillful way. Their eyes, muscles, hands, and feet all work together without awkwardness.

"She's incredibly coordinated — she learned to juggle in just two days."

"Young children aren't yet very coordinated, which is why they trip and spill things so often."

Here the "parts working together" are the systems inside the body — your vision, your sense of balance, your muscles — and when they communicate well with each other, you are coordinated. When they don't, you are uncoordinated, meaning clumsy or awkward.

This meaning is often used with words like well-coordinated, highly coordinated, or naturally coordinated to emphasize the degree.

3. Things that match or go together visually

Less common, but important: coordinated can describe items (especially clothes, furniture, or design elements) that are chosen to look good together — same colour palette, complementary styles, a consistent look.

"She always wears coordinated outfits — the bag, the shoes, and the scarf all match."

"The hotel rooms had coordinated decor: the curtains, pillows, and paintings all followed the same warm, earthy theme."

Here "working together" is about visual harmony rather than action or movement.

Understanding the opposite helps sharpen the meaning.

Uncoordinated means:

  • Actions that are messy, conflicting, or disconnected — "The uncoordinated relief effort meant supplies arrived too late, in the wrong places."
  • A person who lacks body control and moves clumsily — "He's so uncoordinated that he knocked over the lamp just walking past it."
  • Things that clash visually — "Her uncoordinated outfit had three different patterns that didn't work together."
What Makes Something "Coordinated" vs. Just "Organized" or "Planned"?

This is a subtle but important distinction.

  • Organized means things are arranged neatly and in order. You can organize a cupboard on your own.
  • Planned means you have thought ahead about what to do.
  • Coordinated specifically implies multiple separate parts that must all align with each other. It always involves a kind of mutual fitting-together. You can't really "coordinate" one person doing one thing alone — the word only makes full sense when there are multiple elements that need to be brought into harmony.

A well-organized person can work alone. A well-coordinated operation means many actors are in sync.
Common Collocations (Words That Naturally Go With "Coordinated")

Learning which words naturally pair with coordinated will help you use it confidently:

  • A coordinated effort / attack / response / plan / campaign / strategy — multiple forces working in sync
  • A well-coordinated team / operation — emphasizing how smoothly it comes together
  • Coordinated movements — usually refers to physical grace or body control
  • Coordinated colours / outfits / decor — the visual matching sense
  • Highly coordinated — a degree amplifier, used for both physical agility and organized operations
A Few More Examples to Cement the Meaning

"The rescue mission was coordinated across five agencies — each team knew its role, and they communicated in real time."

(Multiple groups working in a planned, synchronized way)

"She's one of the most coordinated athletes I've ever coached — her footwork is flawless."

(Physical grace; body parts working in harmony)

"He bought a coordinated set of bedroom furniture — the bed, the wardrobe, and the nightstand all match perfectly."

(Visual harmony)
The Single Sentence That Captures It All

Coordinated means that multiple separate parts — whether people, actions, muscles, or objects — are working (or have been arranged to work) together in a smooth, harmonious, and purposeful way, so the whole functions better than the parts would on their own.
